# Fairpractice Surprise Billing Disputes (`fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes`)

Tracks No Surprises Act payment disputes: the 30-business-day window to start open negotiation, the 4-business-day window to start IDR after it ends, payments below the payer's own QPA, disputes worth less than the fees, claims that could be batched, and outcomes and fees by payer. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Surprise Billing Disputes never files IDR or sends negotiation notices. Fairpractice Surprise Billing Disputes never accepts settlements.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Money recovery and practice finance · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes demo
npx -y fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up out-of-network emergency group, patients and payers. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`disputes.csv`](fixtures/disputes.csv). Planted (as of November 15, 2026):
  - ER-1001: negotiation ended October 2 and the 4-business-day IDR window closed October 8 with no IDR.
  - ER-1002: open negotiation had to start by October 15 and was never sent.
  - ER-1003: negotiation ended November 10; IDR must start by November 17.
  - ER-1004: open negotiation must start by November 27.
  - ER-1005: paid 400 against a QPA of 900.
  - ER-1006: 40 in dispute against about 465 in fees.
  - ER-1007 and ER-1008: two Cedar Mutual 99291 claims in negotiation that may be batched.
  - ER-0901 (won) and ER-0902 (lost) give outcomes and fees by payer.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 30 and 4 business days, a 10-day warning, a 115 administrative fee and a 350 example entity fee. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `disputes_check` | List missed and coming negotiation and IDR deadlines, payments below QPA, low-value disputes and batching groups, with outcomes by payer. | runs |
| `disputes_write_report` | Write disputes.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and disputes.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/disputes). | runs |
| `disputes_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `disputes_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `disputes_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `disputes_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `idr_initiate` | Fairpractice Surprise Billing Disputes never files IDR or sends negotiation notices. | refused |
| `settlement_accept` | Fairpractice Surprise Billing Disputes never accepts settlements. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `disputes_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `disputes` (required) | Dispute log under --root: claim, patient, payer, code, service date, initial payment or denial date, paid, QPA, our offer, negotiation sent, IDR initiated, outcome, award, fees paid |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: negotiation_days, idr_days, warn_days, admin_fee, entity_fee, qpa_gap_pct, holidays |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Disputes (`disputes`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_id` | text | Claim, Claim ID, Claim #, Claim Number, Encounter, Encounter ID, Visit ID, Invoice |
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `cpt` | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `date` | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `initial_payment_date` | date | Initial Payment Date, Remit Date, Payment Date, Denial Date, ERA Date, Initial Payment |
| `paid` | amount | Paid, Paid Amount, Payment, Insurance Paid, Amount Paid, Allowed Paid |
| `qpa` | amount | QPA, Qualifying Payment Amount, QPA Amount |
| `our_offer` | amount | Our Offer, Offer, Provider Offer, Counteroffer |
| `negotiation_sent` | date | Negotiation Sent, Open Negotiation Sent, Open Negotiation Date, ON Notice Date |
| `idr_initiated` | date | IDR Initiated, IDR Date, IDR Filed, Initiation Date |
| `outcome` | text | Outcome, Status, Result, Determination |
| `award` | amount | Award, Awarded, Determination Amount, Final Amount |
| `fees_paid` | amount | Fees Paid, Fees, IDR Fees, Admin Fee Paid |

## Settings file (`disputes_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `negotiation_days` | Business days for open negotiation (to start it, and its length); default 30 |
| `idr_days` | Business days after negotiation ends to start IDR; default 4 |
| `warn_days` | Business days ahead to warn about the negotiation start deadline; default 10 |
| `admin_fee` | Administrative fee per party per dispute for your year (check CMS); default 115 |
| `entity_fee` | Expected IDR entity fee, for judging low-value disputes; default 0 |
| `qpa_gap_pct` | Percent below the QPA a payment must be to be listed; default 10 |
| `holidays` | Extra non-business days (YYYY-MM-DD) beyond federal holidays |

## Memory

`disputes_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `disputes_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes -- npx -y fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes call disputes_check '{"disputes":"<disputes>"}'
fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-surprise-billing-disputes demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
